concerns.text: The plan cites 'CommonCrawl' (BramVanroy/CommonCrawl-CreativeCommons) as a dataset for 'Natural language domain' ground truth generation. However, the research question requires generating ground-truth optimal block sizes ($B^*$) via an exhaustive sweep of diffusion-based speculative decoding. CommonCrawl is a raw web corpus containing unstructured text, HTML, and noise, lacking the structured prompts and verifiable 'acceptance lengths' required for the sweep logic defined in FR-001. Unlike GSM8K (math problems with solutions) or HumanEval (code with pass/fail tests), CommonCrawl provides no mechanism to validate the 'acceptance length' or determine a correct $B^*$. Using this dataset for the sweep phase renders the ground-truth generation invalid for the stated research question.

The plan assumes the exhaustive sweep (FR-001) can be performed on 'Qwen3-4B' and 'Llama-3-8B' on a GitHub Actions free-tier runner (2 vCPU, ~7 GB RAM). While the plan claims CPU-tractability, running a full diffusion-based speculative decoding sweep (which involves multiple forward passes per sample for different block sizes) on 8B parameter models on a 2-core CPU without GPU acceleration is highly likely to exceed the 6-hour CI limit or cause OOM errors, even with streaming. The feasibility of generating ground truth for 500 samples across 2 architectures and 2 domains within the stated constraints is unverified and likely infeasible with the proposed hardware, risking the entire data generation pipeline.
